papers.abstract: Stochastic order-independent transparency enables efficient and elegant rendering of primitive-based radiance fields like 3D Gaussian Splatting models, but remains impractical due to the inherent visible noise in the output. We propose a principled approach to minimize high-frequency noise, addressing its sources at the representation and image synthesis level. During stochastic rendering, our history-based spatial resampling scheme drastically accelerates image convergence, while temporal importance resampling ensures coherence under camera movement. During training, a color regularizer implicitly reduces the variance along view rays in the 3DGS models. With these properties, our optimized, Vulkan-based renderer effectively mitigates output noise at low and high sample counts, achieving a substantial 13~dB PSNR increase in quality over previous stochastic methods at 1 sample per pixel and quickly converging to sorted 3DGS with an average L1 error of less than $10^{-4}$.
bullets: Targets visible high-frequency noise that limits stochastic order-independent transparency for primitive-based radiance fields.
Uses history-based spatial resampling to accelerate convergence and temporal importance resampling to maintain coherence during camera movement.
Applies a color regularizer during training to reduce variance along view rays in 3DGS models.
An optimized Vulkan renderer improves quality by 13 dB PSNR over prior stochastic methods at 1 sample per pixel.
Converges quickly toward sorted 3DGS, reaching an average L1 error below 10⁻⁴.

papers.abstract: We present Elevator-VIGS, a visual-inertial 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system that keeps tracking and mapping through elevator rides. Inside a moving elevator, the two sensors are in conflict. The camera sees only the robot's motion relative to the elevator, while the IMU senses that motion plus the elevator's motion relative to the world. This conflict is challenging for existing visual-inertial estimators. If vision dominates, the estimator tracks only the robot's motion within the elevator and misses the elevator's rise, and if the conflict remains, the estimator diverges. We observe that the conflict comes from forcing both observations into a single coordinate frame. We instead estimate the robot's pose in the elevator's coordinate frame, and the elevator's motion relative to the world as a per-keyframe transport state, the elevator's rise and vertical velocity, within dense visual-inertial bundle adjustment. Elevator-VIGS detects rides zero-shot with a vision-language model and a depth network, and constrains the transport state at the departure and the arrival. We record real-world and simulated elevator sequences. On these sequences, Elevator-VIGS achieves state-of-the-art tracking and rendering performance. On four elevator-free public benchmarks it keeps the state-of-the-art performance of VIGS-SLAM. Project page: https://ruizhou-cn.github.io/elevator-vigs/.
bullets: Addresses the conflict between camera observations of robot-relative motion and IMU measurements that also include elevator motion.
Estimates robot pose in the elevator frame while modeling elevator transport—rise and vertical velocity—per keyframe.
Detects elevator rides zero-shot using a vision-language model and a depth network.
Constrains transport at elevator departure and arrival within dense visual-inertial bundle adjustment.
Reports state-of-the-art tracking and rendering on elevator sequences while retaining VIGS-SLAM performance on elevator-free benchmarks.

figures.caption: Figure 2: System overview. Elevator-VIGS takes RGB frames and IMU readings as input, tracks the camera online and trains a Gaussian map in parallel, extending VIGS-SLAM with the components outlined in red. Each keyframe, selected by optical flow and initialized through IMU preintegration, holds VIGS-SLAM’s 15-dimensional state of pose, velocity and bias together with its disparities. In the frontend, a ConvGRU refines the dense visual correspondences iteratively, and visual-inertial bundle adjustment optimizes the sliding window at every new keyframe. The ride detector ❺ arms on a semantic and a geometric cue from the RGB frames, and the IMU detects the departure and the arrival within the armed window. From the departure until the fold, each keyframe’s position and velocity decompose into an elevator-frame part and the transport state ❶, the elevator’s rise and vertical velocity. The solve then widens to 17 dimensions, the departure and arrival constraints ❷ constrain the transport state, and the update projection ❸ preserves the transport state through every optimization. Once the keyframes from the elevator leave the sliding window, the deferred fold ❹ writes the rise into the poses and returns them to the world frame. The mapper initializes Gaussians from each new keyframe’s depth and refines the map with color and depth rendering losses. Loop closure proposes keyframe pairs from optical flow, a same-floor gate ❻ rejects pairs on different floors, and each detected loop triggers pose-graph bundle adjustment and a Gaussian update.

papers.abstract: Recovering an object's 3D structure and camera motion from a few uncalibrated views is a fundamental problem in computer vision. Classical structure from motion methods recover 3D geometry consistent with the input images but cannot recover unseen regions; native generation methods produce plausible 3D objects which are related but not necessarily faithful to the input images. Methods simply concatenating reconstruction and generation allow error to cascade across the two stages, instead of producing a 3D object consistent with both the distribution and the input. We propose GenSfM, which integrates image-based 3D reconstruction with a native 3D diffusion model. In particular, we use a multi-modal diffusion transformer to jointly denoise the shape latent and per-view pose latents under shared self-attention, grounding generated geometry in the observed views while using object-level priors to infer unobserved regions. A compact 3D-native UV-volume tokenization keeps the joint sequence small as views are added, and a pose-aware stage refines geometry and texture by sampling per-voxel image features at the recovered camera poses. On Toys4k and GSO, for $4$ uncalibrated views, GenSfM improves novel-view PSNR by $3.2$-$4.5$ dB and reduces median Chamfer distance by $2.8$-$3.8\times$ over a strong native-3D generation baseline, while recovering input-view poses over $96\%$ Acc@$5^\circ$ without any external pose-estimation backbone, post-hoc optimization, or known intrinsics. Project page: https://dotb1ue.github.io/GenSfm/.
authors: Haobin Duan, Binbin Huang, Mochu Xiang, Yiqun Zhao, Zibo Zhao, Yi Ma, Shenghua Gao
bullets: Addresses the gap between classical reconstruction, which misses unseen regions, and unconstrained generation, which may not match inputs.
Uses a multimodal diffusion transformer to jointly denoise shape and per-view pose latents with shared self-attention.
Employs compact 3D-native UV-volume tokens and pose-aware refinement using image features sampled at recovered camera poses.
On Toys4k and GSO with four uncalibrated views, improves novel-view PSNR by 3.2–4.5 dB and reduces median Chamfer distance by 2.8–3.8× versus a native-3D generation baseline.
Recovers input-view poses with over 96% Acc@5° without external pose estimation, post-hoc optimization, or known intrinsics.

papers.abstract: Learning-based structure-from-motion methods such as ACE-Zero have demonstrated strong performance in estimating cameraposes and scene coordinates from unordered image collections without requiring ground truth supervision. However, the lack of global and multi-view consistency constraints in ACE-Zero can lead to pose drift and misalignment, particularly in complex or ambiguous scenes. In this work, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates pose graph optimization (PGO) into ACE-Zero to refine camera poses and suppress incorrect refinements. We construct pose graphs directly from ACE-Zero outputs by extracting relative pose constraints from predicted scene coordinates. Furthermore, we introduce an uncertainty-aware optimization strategy by estimating confidence scores using geometric priors, including epipolar and optical flow consistencies across views. Our approach improves the robustness and accuracy of pose estimation, demonstrating that global geometric reasoning can effectively complement learning-based inference in structure-from-motion.
authors: Tze Ho Elden Tse, Jizong Peng, Angela Yao
bullets: Addresses pose drift and multi-view misalignment caused by limited global consistency in ACE-Zero.
Builds pose graphs from ACE-Zero-predicted scene coordinates and relative pose constraints.
Uses uncertainty-aware optimization with confidence scores from epipolar and optical-flow consistency.
Reports improved pose-estimation robustness and accuracy through global geometric reasoning.
Scope: targets unordered image collections and ambiguous or complex scenes.

papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a promising representation for real-time novel view synthesis and 3D scene reconstruction. For practical deployment, recent studies have explored pose-free feed-forward 3DGS, which reconstructs Gaussian representations directly from unposed input images. However, these methods remain sensitive to residual pose errors, which perturb canonical-space Gaussian transformation, introducing noisy supervision for geometry and attribute learning. To address this problem, we present SG-Splat, a pose-free feed-forward 3DGS framework that improves robustness to pose uncertainty and stabilizes the learning of Gaussian primitives. SG-Splat decouples geometry estimation and Gaussian attribute prediction into two dedicated branches, reducing error coupling between pose-sensitive geometry and Gaussian attributes. We further introduce a coarse-to-fine refinement pipeline, consisting of Flow-Guided Pose Refinement (FGPR) and Residual-Guided Geometry Correction (RGC), to improve geometric alignment before Gaussian attribute reconstruction. Specifically, FGPR refines camera poses with flow-based correlation features and differentiable bundle adjustment. RGC then corrects initial point maps using depth residuals derived from FGPR, producing more reliable Gaussian centers. To stabilize training, we introduce a dual-path strategy that mixes ground-truth and predicted poses for canonical transformation. It provides clean supervision for Gaussian attributes while improving geometry robustness to residual pose errors. Extensive experiments on DL3DV and RealEstate10K show that SG-Splat achieves state-of-the-art performance in both novel view synthesis and pose estimation.
authors: Xiaohan Lu, Jiaqi Zhang, Weijia Jiang, Siwei Ma
bullets: Targets noisy geometric and attribute supervision caused by residual pose errors in unposed input images.
Uses separate branches for geometry estimation and Gaussian attribute prediction to reduce error coupling.
Applies coarse-to-fine refinement through Flow-Guided Pose Refinement and Residual-Guided Geometry Correction.
Uses a dual-path strategy mixing ground-truth and predicted poses to stabilize training and improve robustness.
Reports state-of-the-art novel view synthesis and pose estimation on DL3DV and RealEstate10K.

figures.caption: Fig. 2. Overview of the pipeline. The input images are processed by separate geometry and attribute branches. The geometry branch predicts initial local point maps and camera poses through the point head and camera head, while the attribute branch predicts the remaining Gaussian attributes. Flow-Guided Pose Refinement (FGPR) refines the initial poses and produces depth residuals, which are used by Residual-Guided Geometry Correction (RGC) to correct the local Gaussian centers µlocal . The corrected centers are transformed into the canonical space with the refined poses and combined with the predicted attributes to form the final Gaussian representation.

Fig. 6. Qualitative comparisons on the DL3DV dataset with 24 input views. With more accurate camera pose estimation, our model produces geometrically consistent Gaussian primitives, yielding sharper boundaries, finer details, and fewer artifacts in novel views.

Fig. 7. Qualitative comparisons on the RealEstate10K dataset with sparse-view inputs (6 views). Even with only a few input views, our model reconstructs more coherent scene geometry and more realistic novel views, with clearer details and reduced artifacts.

Fig. 1. Comparison of pose usage strategies in pose-free feed-forward 3DGS training. (a) AnySplat [1] uses predicted poses with pose supervision, maintaining consistency between training and inference but suffering from perturbations caused by pose errors. (b) WorldMirror [2] uses ground-truth poses with pose supervision, stabilizing training but introducing inconsistency between training and inference. (c) E-RayZer [3] relies on predicted poses without pose supervision, making optimization sensitive to pose errors. (d) Our method uses mixed poses with pose supervision, balancing stable learning and robustness to residual pose errors.

Fig. 5. Dual-Path Training Strategy. The refined predicted pose and the ground-truth (GT) pose are sampled with equal probability. The selected pose is used to transform local Gaussian centers into the canonical space for rendering. When the ground-truth pose is selected, reliable rendering supervision updates both the geometry and attribute branches. When the predicted pose is selected, rendering gradients are detached from the attribute branch and only the optimize geometry branch. This asymmetric optimization stabilizes attribute learning while improving geometry robustness under residual pose errors.

Fig. 3. Flow-Guided Pose Refinement (FGPR). At each iteration, FGPR uses the current pose and geometry estimates to build flow-based correlation features and optical flow of camera motion. Together with context features, these cues are fed into an update operator to predict correspondence corrections ∆pij . The corrected correspondences p∗ ij are optimized by differentiable bundle adjustment (DBA) to jointly update camera poses and depths. Over T iterations, FGPR progressively improves pose accuracy and produces depth residuals for subsequent geometry correction.

Fig. 4. Residual-Guided Geometry Correction (RGC). RGC uses the residual depth map ∆D̂i from FGPR to correct the initial local point map M̂i. The residual depth map and the initial point map are embedded and fused with geometry tokens to predict a bounded multiplicative correction, producing the corrected point map M̃i.

papers.abstract: Voronoi tessellations have recently emerged as an adaptive, space-partitioning discretization for shape and appearance reconstruction from multi-view images. However, the irregular cells they produce make the repeated reconstruction of the tessellation during optimization costly. We therefore explore adaptive centroidal Voronoi tessellations (CVTs), which extend standard CVTs with non-uniform cell sizes while preserving the regular, well-shaped cells that make them efficient to compute. In CVTSplat, cell size is modulated by the evolving signed distance field, concentrating sites near the zero level set while keeping cells nearly centroidal. This regularity lets us specialize the whole pipeline, with GPU algorithms for nearest-neighbor queries and approximate Voronoi construction, and a rasterizer tailored to small, nearly isotropic cells. Our Voronoi construction is 5 to 10 times faster than general-purpose alternatives in this regime. On DTU and BlendedMVS, CVTSplat reaches geometric accuracy competitive with the best Gaussian-splatting surface methods while training in about 2.5 minutes on a single GPU.
authors: Briac Toussaint, Diego Thomas, Jean-S\'ebastien Franco, Edmond Boyer, Christian Theobalt
bullets: Targets the high cost of repeatedly reconstructing irregular Voronoi tessellations during optimization.
Modulates cell sizes using the evolving signed distance field, concentrating sites near the zero level set while maintaining near-centroidal cells.
Introduces GPU-optimized nearest-neighbor queries, approximate Voronoi construction, and rasterization for small, nearly isotropic cells.
The specialized Voronoi construction is reported as 5–10× faster than general-purpose alternatives in this setting.
Achieves competitive geometric accuracy with leading Gaussian-splatting surface methods on DTU and BlendedMVS, with training taking about 2.5 minutes on one GPU.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Overview of our approach during optimization. Top row: Construction of the tessellation. (a) The sites are processed to obtain a list of their 32 nearest neighbors, (b) before building the Voronoi diagram as an adjacency graph. (c) The center of mass of each cell is then computed to regularize the distribution of the sites via the CVT loss. (d) The Voronoi diagram is optionally converted to a Delaunay triangulation to extract the zero-level set with marching tetrahedra. Bottom row: Differentiable volume rendering from posed images. (e) The sites’ attributes (learnable SDF and features) are smoothed with a Gaussian kernel. (f) The gradient of the SDF is also computed to produce normal vectors, which define a piecewise linear SDF over the cells. Then, for all viewpoints in the mini-batch, (g) a per-site color is computed based on the camera’s position, (h) before rasterizing the scene and comparing against the ground-truth image.

Figure 13: We remove one loss on each example to ablate our model. Bottom: The multi-view (ZNCC), depth and normal losses as well as the reflection probes are important for geometric accuracy. Figure 5: The 2D inequalities enclose the feasibility region, which corresponds to a facet of the polyhedron wrapping the cell. Each line is the intersection of the reference plane P𝑟 with another bisector plane P𝑗 .

Figure 3: Left: The volume and centroid of the cell are computed by casting rays from the site’s location. Right: Our biased CVT loss maintains the sites slightly closer to the implicit surface than the centroids x̄, resulting in stretched cells along the SDF gradient.

The blue one queries KNN at each site while the red one queries at the cell centroid computed at the previous update. Left: Number of Voronoi neighbors per site. The mean is ≈ 14.2, corresponding to 14 bisector planes contributing to each cell on average. papers.abstract: Monocular occupancy prediction in indoor scenes aims to recover a scene's 3D geometry and semantics from a single RGB image. Existing methods are restricted to a closed set of predefined categories, limiting their ability to generalize to unseen categories. This limitation is particularly critical in indoor scenes, where objects exhibit highly diverse and fine-grained semantic categories. We study open-vocabulary monocular occupancy prediction for indoor scenes and present OVM-Occ, a Gaussian-based occupancy framework with an instance-aware vision-language teacher. Specifically, we adopt Language-Embedded Gaussians as the intermediate scene representation, propose a geometry-aware deformable attention module to refine Gaussian semantic features, and construct instance-level vision-language embeddings to provide reliable semantic supervision. We further introduce geometry-aware decoupled semantic distillation to mitigate the interference between geometry learning and semantic learning. To evaluate open-vocabulary occupancy prediction performance, we introduce OpenOcc-ScanNet and OpenOcc-Replica, two extended benchmarks with more diverse and fine-grained semantic categories. Experiments show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in open-vocabulary monocular occupancy prediction for indoor scenes, outperforming the previous state-of-the-art approach by 12.2 mIoU and 0.6 IoU on the Occ-ScanNet dataset, with consistent gains under new open-vocabulary evaluation protocols.
authors: Shuyang Yu, Haibo Qin, Shaohan Hu, Wei Shan, Xiaoqing Guan, You Wang, Guang Li
bullets: Addresses the limited category generalization of existing closed-set monocular occupancy methods.

papers.abstract: Recent studies on generalizable human Gaussian splatting have achieved the notable progress in synthesizing novel views of unseen human subjects from multi-view images. Despite this progress, existing methods still struggle to represent fine-grained details of human subjects, which inherently involve high geometric and textural complexity. This is because previous methods do not impose a constraint on how densely Gaussians are placed, which often leads to blurry rendering results in complex regions. To address this problem, we propose a complexity-guided regularization scheme. The key idea is to leverage a complexity prior computed via the local entropy in geometric and textural characteristics of a clothed human. This effectively prevents Gaussians from being coarsely placed in complex regions, which facilitates the faithful reconstruction of intricate structures. Furthermore, we sample local patches predominantly from complex regions according to this complexity prior, which allows the model to be sufficiently supervised by local details. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method delivers state-of-the-art performance while maintaining the real-time inference speed in generalizable human Gaussian splatting. The code and model are publicly available at https://github.com/DCVL-3D/CGR-GS_release.
authors: Gun Ryu, Gi-Mun Um, Won-Sik Cheong, Wonjun Kim
bullets: Targets blurry rendering of fine-grained geometric and textural details in unseen human subjects.
Uses local entropy to estimate complexity in clothed-human geometry and appearance.
Regularizes Gaussian placement to prevent overly coarse representations in complex regions.
Samples local training patches preferentially from high-complexity areas for stronger detail supervision.
Reports state-of-the-art benchmark performance with real-time inference; code and models are publicly available.

papers.abstract: A cooperative 3D detector can miss a vehicle even when the LiDAR points on it remain unchanged. We study this failure under adverse weather as Weather-Induced Context Interference. To our knowledge, this is the first controlled study of how weather-related exterior changes remove cooperative benefits while preserving all points inside annotated objects. Controlled experiments on simulated and real roadside inputs show that exterior loss changes object representations before fusion and removes previously useful assistance. On real inputs, restoring object-neighborhood features recovers 30 of 31 induced failures; three equal-area exterior controls recover none. The failure condition also appears with a second fusion model. These findings motivate Adverse-Weather Cooperative Repair (AWCR), with separate implementations for the available supervision. Point Classifier filters added weather returns in simulation. On real inputs, Local Correction refines candidates and Quality Selection checks them against current measurements, without naturally paired clear/adverse-weather recordings. Candidate tracing shows that correction supplies accurate geometry for some targets that original candidates cannot localize at the evaluation threshold. On natural adverse-weather CoInfra development data, AWCR improves car bird's-eye-view (BEV) AP@0.7 by 4.66 points with V2X-ViT and 5.56 with AttFuse. On simulated V2X-R fog, it improves vehicle BEV AP@0.7 by 4.47 points at a fixed 4,096-candidate budget.
bullets: Identifies Weather-Induced Context Interference: unchanged object LiDAR points can still yield missed detections when exterior context is altered.
Controlled simulated and real-roadside experiments show exterior loss damages object representations before fusion and removes useful cooperative assistance.
Restoring object-neighborhood features recovers 30 of 31 induced failures, while equal-area exterior controls recover none; the effect also appears with another fusion model.
AWCR uses Point Classifier for simulation and Local Correction plus Quality Selection for real inputs, adapting to different supervision settings.
AWCR improves car BEV AP@0.7 by 4.66 points with V2X-ViT and 5.56 with AttFuse on natural adverse-weather data, and by 4.47 points on simulated fog.

papers.abstract: Monocular depth estimation has advanced rapidly with the development of foundation models that demonstrate strong zero-shot generalisation across diverse visual domains. However, the applicability of these models to visual perception for lower-limb prosthetics remains largely unexplored. Reliable depth perception is particularly important for prosthesis users, who often experience significant challenges when navigating stairs, uneven terrain, and other complex environments. To address this gap, we introduce the Lower-Limb Prosthesis (LP) dataset, a benchmark designed to evaluate depth perception from an emulated knee-level prosthetic viewpoint. Using this dataset, we evaluate four state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation foundation models. Our results provide the first systematic benchmark of monocular depth estimation performance from a prosthetic viewpoint, while highlighting both the challenges and the potential of deploying foundation models in prosthetic perception systems. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Ishivijay/lp_dataset.
authors: Ishi Vijayvergiya, Marc H\"olle, Youssef Dawoud, Amir El-Ghoussani, Michele De Vita, Rohan Asthana, Philipp Beckerle, Vasileios Belagiannis

Provides a first systematic benchmark of depth estimation from a prosthetic viewpoint.

papers.abstract: Sparse-view 4D reconstruction is highly under-constrained when only a few cameras are available. Generative priors can recover missing appearances, but video models are computationally impractical for iterative reconstruction, whereas single-view models produce temporally inconsistent pseudo-observations. Moreover, directly absorbing uncertain generative outputs into Gaussian optimization often creates redundant primitives and floating artifacts. To address these challenges, we propose DUET4D, a self-corrective coupled guidance framework for sparse-view 4D Gaussian splatting. The core of our approach is a self-corrective framework where the 4D representation guides generative prior for spatio-temporal consistent supervisions. We first construct sequential alignments from current Gaussian evidence to steer the latent restoration. Then we use Sequential Fidelity Resampling to lift generative supervisions into Gaussian space to selectively distinguish repeatedly supported primitives. The corrected representation then provides more reliable Gaussian evidence for the next restoration cycle. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DUET4D significantly improves rendering quality and rendering efficiency.
authors: Beizhen Zhao, Nanjie Yao, Boyi Fu, Qingsong Yan, Haofan Ren, Kaiyong Zhao, Hao Wang
bullets: Addresses the under-constrained nature of 4D reconstruction from only a few cameras.
Uses sequential alignment to guide latent generative restoration with current Gaussian evidence.
Introduces Sequential Fidelity Resampling to transfer generative supervision selectively into Gaussian space.
Iteratively corrects the representation to reduce redundant primitives and floating artifacts.
Experiments report improved rendering quality and efficiency.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Qualitative comparisons of state-of-the-art methods. Visual differences are highlighted with red insets for better clarity. Our approach outperforms other models on different scenes, demonstrating advantages in challenging scenarios. Best viewed in color.

Then we design a training-free anchor-driven latent steering mechanism within the latent space of SDM for temporally consistent generative outputs. The frames and confidence map will be used to locate Gaussians with weak spatial and temporal consistency for optimization. The reserved Gaussians are controlled by a spatial grid and Fourier spline priors for motion smoothness and regularization.

papers.abstract: Camera-based bird's-eye view (BEV) perception methods such as Fast-BEV have demonstrated promising results with fast inference speed and competitive accuracy. However, their robustness to real-world corruptions remains insufficiently explored, posing risks for autonomous driving deployment where environmental variations are inevitable. In this paper, we propose Sparse Recovery Bird's-Eye View Model Soup (SR-BEVS), a sparse recovery learning approach that simultaneously improves clean accuracy and corruption robustness without requiring additional data or architectural modifications. Our method identifies pruning candidates based on layer-wise weight magnitudes, applies random pruning to create diverse sparse models, and retrains each model with a randomly sampled learning rate. By averaging these diverse recovered models into a single dense model, we achieve enhanced robustness against various corruptions while introducing zero inference overhead. We further provide a mode connectivity analysis demonstrating that our pruning-based diversification preserves the connected low-loss basin necessary for stable weight averaging. Experiments on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate up to 33.8% improvement in corruption robustness and a 1.8% gain in clean accuracy over the Fast-BEV baseline, with consistent improvements across sensor noise, weather distortions, and illumination changes. Our simple yet effective approach may be applicable to other BEV models.
authors: Jinwoo Chung, Sangho An, Hyunsung Park, Jangho Kim
bullets: Targets insufficient robustness of camera-based BEV detection under real-world corruptions.
Prunes weights by layer-wise magnitude, randomly sparsifies models, retrains them with varied learning rates, and averages the recovered models.
Mode connectivity analysis suggests pruning-based diversity preserves a stable low-loss basin for weight averaging.
On nuScenes, reports up to 33.8% better corruption robustness and 1.8% higher clean accuracy than Fast-BEV.
Improvements cover sensor noise, weather distortions, and illumination changes; applicability beyond BEV models is suggested but not established.

papers.abstract: Dynamic Gaussian reconstruction requires compact scene features to support coordinated changes in geometry and appearance. A factorized grid provides efficient local queries, but accurate interpolation alone does not ensure that the resulting dynamic attributes remain compatible across space and time. We introduce DimFlow, a framework that learns these features through bidirectional interaction between a multi-resolution grid and a coordinate-based expert branch. Feature-level adversarial alignment connects their distributions, adaptive fusion transfers complementary information, and activation-masked residual feedback refines the grid during training. Four attribute experts organize deformation, rotation, opacity, and temporal information before Gaussian rendering. In the aggregate comparison across D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, and DAVIS, DimFlow achieves 39.73 dB PSNR, improving on 4D-GS by 1.92 dB while matching its reported 85 FPS rendering speed. The model occupies 18.9 MB, compared with 18.3 MB for 4D-GS. Component and attribute-expert ablations reveal complementary contributions from feature alignment, adaptive exchange, and temporal processing.
bullets: Targets spatially and temporally compatible dynamic attributes beyond what grid interpolation alone provides.
Uses feature-level adversarial alignment, adaptive fusion, and activation-masked residual feedback between grid and expert branches.
Employs four experts for deformation, rotation, opacity, and temporal information before Gaussian rendering.
Reports 39.73 dB PSNR across D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, and DAVIS—1.92 dB above 4D-GS—with 85 FPS rendering.
Ablations indicate complementary benefits from feature alignment, adaptive exchange, and temporal processing.

papers.abstract: Recent multi-view Transformers (e.g., DUSt3R and VGGT) have advanced 3D reconstruction by scaling training data and model capacity from two views to many views and long sequences, subsuming the classical SfM/SLAM pipeline of feature extraction, matching, and pose estimation in a single feed-forward pass. Yet this subsumption hides the interfaces between pipeline stages---correspondences, geometry, and pose are entangled in a single forward pass, leaving supervised fine-tuning as the major path to improvement and offering no mechanism to correct predictions from geometric evidence at test time. We propose PosePlaner to close this gap by reviving the classical coupling between correspondences and pose via flow matching, treating pose refinement as a conditional generation problem that takes coarse geometric matches and initial pose as input condition and fuses the resulting pose hypotheses into a single refined estimate, providing a continuous, data-driven analog of RANSAC voting. Our method is trained efficiently on two-view data, yet serves as a periodic refiner for streaming n-view pose estimators with no retraining. Empirically, it corrects failures of feed-forward predictors, substantially improves correspondence-based solvers, and reduces accumulated drift in long streaming sequences.
authors: Yihang Chen, Bin Tan, Yujun Shen, Yinghao Xu, Nan Xue
bullets: Addresses the entanglement of correspondences, geometry, and pose in modern multi-view Transformers.
Conditions pose refinement on coarse geometric matches and an initial pose, then fuses pose hypotheses into one estimate.
Provides a continuous, data-driven analogue of RANSAC voting.
Trained efficiently on two-view data and used as a periodic refiner for streaming multi-view pose estimators without retraining.
Corrects feed-forward failures, improves correspondence-based solvers, and reduces drift in long sequences.

papers.abstract: Visual captures provide detailed scene appearance, but converting them into interactive simulation environments requires object reconstruction, physical modeling, and correction of intermediate errors. We present SceneAgent, an agentic pipeline that coordinates these steps through simulator-based visual inspection and repair. The pipeline processes 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), photogrammetry, LiDAR captures, AI-generated 3DGS scenes, and 4D videos of dynamic scenes, and combines object segmentation, physical parameter estimation, part decomposition, articulation, and deformable simulation. To support policy learning, SceneAgent generates diverse object variants ("digital sisters") and scripted demonstrations. On a cluttered bin scene from GraspClutter6D, SceneAgent raises F1 at 1 cm for every coding agent with scorable outputs both with and without its skills, and its reconstructions are better than SimFoundry: all agent configurations exceed SimFoundry's F1 score, with a best of 60.75% versus 6.9%. On three dynamic scenes from 4DCodeBench, SceneAgent raises the mean dynamic IoU of Gemini 4 Argon from 0.86% to 99.09%. We further demonstrate diverse simulated interactions and preliminary policy transfer to a real robot.
authors: Luke Hollis, Tianxing Fan, Heng Yang
bullets: Addresses the challenge of turning 3D/4D captures into usable simulation environments with accurate geometry and physics.
Coordinates segmentation, physical parameter estimation, part decomposition, articulation, and deformable simulation using simulator-based visual feedback.
Supports 3DGS, photogrammetry, LiDAR, AI-generated scenes, and 4D dynamic captures.
Generates diverse object variants (“digital sisters”) and scripted demonstrations for policy learning.
Improves reported reconstruction metrics substantially on cluttered and dynamic-scene benchmarks, with preliminary transfer to a real robot.

papers.title: SceneAgent: An Agentic Pipeline from 3D and 4D Captures to Simulation Environments

papers.abstract: Driving video captured through a windshield violates the world-space consistency assumed by 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS): the road scene exhibits parallax while cabin reflections remain attached to the camera, causing standard 3DGS to embed reflected content into the reconstructed scene. We introduce RIDE-Splat, a pipeline for reflection-free 3D reconstruction from posed driving video without clean images, reflection masks, or pretrained networks. RIDE-Splat assigns world-consistent transmission through the windshield to a 3DGS scene and the dominant camera-attached reflection to one shared, signed RGB image. It builds the clean reconstruction in two passes. First, it learns the 3D geometry and the signed reflection image, representing both added radiance and transmission attenuation. Then, it uses the reflection-removed training images to fit a clean 3DGS model. At inference, the reflection image is discarded, preserving the standard 3DGS rendering path. We also introduce the RIDE-Splat Dataset, the first 3D reconstruction benchmark for reflection removal from driving video -- with real driving scenes, physical windshield reflections in training views, and separately captured non-reflective evaluation images. Across the RIDE-Splat Dataset, XLD, and Wayve, RIDE-Splat outperforms 3DGS, DC-Gaussian, and RobustSplat on all nine aggregate metrics, improving PSNR by up to 3.59 dB and reducing LPIPS by up to 0.0876. We achieve the highest metrics in 38 out of 42 per-scene comparisons and removes windshield reflections that remain visible in the baselines while preserving the transmitted scene.
authors: Kevin David Hayes, Alex Hanson, Allen Tu, Pranav Asthana, Matthias Zwicker, Tom Goldstein
bullets: Addresses the mismatch between world-consistent road scenes and camera-attached windshield reflections in 3DGS.
Jointly models scene transmission with 3D Gaussians and dominant reflections using a shared signed RGB image.
Uses a two-pass process: estimate geometry and reflections, then fit a clean 3DGS model to reflection-removed images.
Introduces the RIDE-Splat Dataset with real driving scenes, physical reflections, and separate non-reflective evaluation views.
Outperforms the compared baselines across nine aggregate metrics on RIDE-Splat, XLD, and Wayve; reflection removal preserves the transmitted scene.

figures.caption: Fig. 2: Overview of RIDE-Splat. Given posed driving frames with windshield reflections, RIDE-Splat reconstructs a reflection-free 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scene without paired clean images or reflection masks. Phase I: Coordinate-Based Joint Optimization (Sec. III-B) warms up scene geometry, then jointly separates a world-consistent 3DGS scene from a shared, signed 2D reflection layer. Phase II: Reflection Self-Localization (Sec. III-C) derives a continuous spatial weight from the recovered reflection layer and retrains the decomposition from scratch with this support fixed, preventing weak scene residuals from entering the final reconstruction. This refit adds no optimized parameters. At inference, the reflection layer is discarded and standard 3DGS rasterization renders reflection-free novel views.

papers.abstract: Significant advancements in 3D asset creation have enabled high-fidelity 3D generation from images. However, most existing representations remain inherently static, lacking the ability to model physically plausible behaviors under dynamic interactions. We present \textbf{PhysCreator}, a unified framework that directly generates simulation-ready 3D representations with spatially varying physical properties from images. Unlike prior approaches that treat physical attributes as simple post-hoc predictions or rely on expensive per-instance optimization, we reformulate physical property estimation within a unified 3D representation learning framework. We introduce a voxel-aligned latent space by lifting image observations into a spatially structured 3D representation, in which geometry, appearance, and physical properties are jointly modeled and inferred in a feed-forward manner. To enable scalable learning without densely annotated physical ground truth, we leverage vision-language distillation to transfer material-aware semantic priors from powerful vision-language models into spatially grounded voxel-level supervision. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior visual quality, physical plausibility, and generalization compared to prior approaches.
authors: Shiyan Zheng, Ming Li, Lei Han, Xiangyu Xu
bullets: Addresses the limitation of static 3D representations that cannot model physically plausible behavior under interaction.
Uses a voxel-aligned latent space to jointly infer geometry, appearance, and physical properties.
Applies vision-language distillation to provide spatially grounded, material-aware supervision without dense physical annotations.
Experiments report improved visual quality, physical plausibility, and generalization over prior approaches.

Bottom: To provide scalable supervision, vision-language distillation generates part-level semantic and physical annotations, which are lifted into voxel-level labels for training the physical-material decoder. The predicted geometry and physical properties are then passed to an MPM simulator to evaluate and visualize dynamic behavior.

Our method enables the joint prediction of geometry and physically meaningful attributes, such as material type, stiffness, and density, with strong generalization across diverse objects. The generated 3D Gaussians can be seamlessly integrated into simulations, yielding realistic and dynamic physical behaviors.

papers.abstract: Non-rigid structure from motion (NRSfM) aims to recover camera motion and time-varying 3D shape from tracked 2D image measurements. Recent high-performing methods show that shape-space factorization remains highly effective for this task. These methods often use costly solvers for two key steps. First, a semidefinite programming (SDP) cone solver to perform Euclidean correction. Next, an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) solver to recover the low-rank shape. These steps often scale poorly to long sequences and dense point tracks. We propose a fast, scalable NRSfM solver that avoids these costly steps. For rotation estimation, we introduce a differentiable Euclidean correction that directly optimizes small factors for each sequence. A row-polar projection then maps each estimated camera block to the closest row-orthonormal matrix. For shape estimation, we introduce an unrolled spectral-proximal solver. It combines reprojection-gradient steps with weighted singular-value shrinkage in the reshuffled shape domain. This solver further uses FISTA-style restart and continuation. The spectral shrinkage operator itself is classical, but we embed it in a fixed differentiable solver, while preserving NRSfM's geometric constraints. The proposed approach is category-agnostic, requires no external training data, and maps naturally to modern accelerator-friendly linear algebra primitives. Across sparse, dense, noisy, missing-data, and long-sequence benchmarks, our solver achieves substantial speedups with competitive reconstruction accuracy, including 7x-1000x runtime improvements on dense sequences with 28,887 tracked points.
bullets: Targets the poor scalability of conventional Euclidean-correction and low-rank-shape solvers for long sequences and dense tracks.
Estimates camera rotations by directly optimizing small factors, followed by row-polar projection to enforce row-orthonormality.
Recovers shape with an unrolled spectral-proximal solver combining reprojection gradients, weighted singular-value shrinkage, FISTA-style restart, and continuation.
Works across sparse, dense, noisy, and missing-data settings without external training data.
Reports 7×–1000× runtime improvements on dense sequences with up to 28,887 tracked points while maintaining competitive accuracy.

papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a standard representation for real-time novel-view synthesis. Yet, its quality-efficiency trade-off still relies heavily on adaptive density control. Existing cloning, splitting, and pruning rules use proxy signals, such as position gradients, opacity, and image-space error. Although effective in practice, these signals do not directly answer the structural question behind density control: where should new Gaussians be allocated to reduce the multi-view reconstruction loss, and which existing primitives can be pruned with minimal penalty. To address this, we propose first-variation birth-death control for 3DGS, a principled approach that replaces heuristic structural decisions with a variational score derived from the reconstruction loss. At each structural update, we freeze the current Gaussian population, attach auxiliary mass coordinates to each primitive, and differentiate the multiview loss with respect to these coordinates. We demonstrate that this score is a coordinate of the first variation of the Splat Regression Model, giving a rigorous local descent surrogate for birth-death moves: high-score Gaussians are selected as birth sites, while low-score, low-opacity Gaussians are selected for removal. Across standard 3DGS benchmarks, integrating this score into 3DGS-MCMC yields state-of-the-art reconstruction quality and outperforms existing methods, delivering the most significant gains under tight Gaussian budgets. Ultimately, our work provides compelling evidence that gradient-based variational metrics offer a principled alternative to proxy heuristics in 3DGS.
authors: Quan Tran Hong, Long Nguyen-Chi, Binh T. Nguyen
bullets: Targets the problem of deciding where to add Gaussians and which to prune to reduce multiview reconstruction loss.
Introduces first-variation birth-death control using loss gradients with respect to auxiliary mass coordinates attached to each Gaussian.
Uses high-score Gaussians as birth sites and removes low-score, low-opacity primitives.
Integrated into 3DGS-MCMC, the method achieves state-of-the-art quality on standard 3DGS benchmarks and outperforms existing approaches.
The reported benefits are strongest when the number of Gaussians is tightly constrained.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of the score-guided birth–death controller. At each structural update, we freeze the current Gaussian parameters and expose one auxiliary mass coordinate per primitive, implemented as ai(x) 7→ miai(x). A batched multiview backward pass computes the first-variation score qi = −∂F̂t(m)/∂mi|m=1. Higher scores explicitly predict a larger first-order loss reduction from assigning mass to that primitive. Guided by these scores, the controller kills low-opacity, low-score slots and births new capacity at high-score parent sites using the 3DGS-MCMC transitions.

papers.abstract: We propose a novel method for robust point cloud registration with only one tunable parameter. Our method, dubbed TLP, uses truncated $L_p$ functions with different values of $p$ to assign priority scores to correspondences, select the hypothesis, and refine the final model. By leveraging the robustness of truncated functions, TLP effectively handles the high outlier rates commonly encountered in real-world 3D feature matching. We also exploit GPU parallelization to evaluate hypotheses efficiently, enabling registration from thousands of correspondences in under a second on average. With only one tunable parameter, our method offers greater practicality than multi-parameter methods that require dataset-specific tuning of several parameters. Evaluations on public benchmark datasets demonstrate that TLP achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art single-parameter methods. Furthermore, it outperforms two widely used multi-parameter methods on three of the four evaluated datasets while maintaining competitive runtime.
authors: Seong Hun Lee, Patrick Vandewalle, Javier Civera
bullets: Addresses high outlier rates in real-world 3D feature matching.
Uses truncated $L_p$ functions to prioritize correspondences, select hypotheses, and refine the final model.
GPU parallelization evaluates thousands of correspondences in under a second on average.
Outperforms state-of-the-art single-parameter methods and beats two multi-parameter methods on three of four benchmark datasets.
Offers practical tuning with competitive runtime, though performance varies across evaluated datasets.

papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a promising approach for fast, high-quality novel-view rendering. However, its large parameter size remains a bottleneck for storage and transmission. We propose RacerGS, a compact 3DGS compression framework that achieves scene reconstruction at significantly reduced storage sizes with preserved fidelity. To obtain compact and spatially coherent features, we design a hash projection model that projects the anchor hash encodings into compact context features. Additionally, we introduce a FiLM-modulated autoregressive GRU context model that utilizes causal dependencies among anchor feature groups and uses recurrent hidden states to refine entropy-model parameters, improving bitrate efficiency. Furthermore, we adaptively entropy-code quantized anchor-attribute residuals relative to their context-predicted means, leveraging spatial consistency to reduce symbol entropy. Overall, RacerGS achieves more than 150x compression over vanilla 3DGS and 28x over Scaffold-GS, while providing comparable rendering quality. Extensive experiments across five datasets demonstrate that RacerGS outperforms prior 3DGS compression methods in both storage reduction and rate-distortion performance.
authors: Wenqing Wang, Huimin Zeng, Yun Fu
bullets: Addresses the large storage and transmission cost of 3DGS.
Projects anchor hash encodings into compact, spatially coherent context features.
Uses a FiLM-modulated autoregressive GRU to model causal dependencies and refine entropy parameters.
Entropy-codes quantized anchor-attribute residuals relative to context-predicted means.
Reports over 150× compression versus vanilla 3DGS and 28× versus Scaffold-GS, with comparable quality across five datasets.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Pipeline overview. RacerGS compresses 3DGS through three components: (1) a hash projection model maps hash encodings fh i to compact spatial context features f c i ; (2) adaptive residual quantization encodes anchor attributes relative to context-predicted means using learned quantization steps; (3) an autoregressive GRU summarizes previously decoded feature chunks, followed by FiLM modulation and a shared predictor conditioned on base statistics and chunk embeddings. The refined parameters are combined with the spatial prior to form an accurate Gaussian mixture model for residual entropy coding.

papers.abstract: Scalable 3D Gaussian Splatting allows one scene representation to serve different Gaussian-count budgets, yet its quality-budget curve may lag behind models optimized separately for each budget. Reducing the number of Gaussians changes both the selected members and the reconstruction tasks carried by the survivors; parameters inherited from a high-budget model may fit a low-budget representation poorly. We propose ParetoGS, which describes member changes and parameter evolution with a small set of adapted budget anchors and decodes intermediate budgets without separate optimization at every requested count. ParetoGS alternates pruning and fixed-member adaptation to build nested anchors with persistent identities, and encodes their parameter changes relative to the full model in a compact residual atlas. At decoding, it interpolates the states of shared members and gradually introduces the rendering contributions of new members, connecting sparse anchors into a continuous-budget representation. Across 13 scenes, ParetoGS attains better average PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS with fewer Gaussians than the compared prefix methods at 10% of each method's own full model. From a shared full model, it also outperforms FlexGS-imp at its trained 1%, 5%, and 10% budgets and NanoGS-imp at the 1% and 0.1% budgets. On Garden, its non-anchor quality approaches an empirical reference from independently optimized GNS models at higher retention ratios and exceeds it at some lower-budget points. Across 13 scenes, encoding reduces mean additional state from 390.0 to 85.7 MB with an average PSNR change of 0.01 dB. Project page: https://xiaobin2001.github.io/ParetoGS-Web/
authors: Xiaobin Deng, Changyu Diao, Min Li, Duanqing Xu
bullets: Addresses quality degradation when pruning a high-budget Gaussian model for lower budgets, where surviving parameters may no longer fit well.

Across 13 scenes, improves average PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS over prefix methods at 10% retention and outperforms several budget-trained baselines at selected budgets.
Reduces mean additional encoding state from 390.0 MB to 85.7 MB with only a 0.01 dB average PSNR change.

(c) For a requested count K between adjacent anchors L and U , decoding interpolates sharedmember parameters and introduces K−L entering members from U with opacity gating, producing a standard K-Gaussian model.

papers.abstract: High-resolution 3D Gaussian Splatting training increases pixel and Gaussian-tile intersection counts, expanding rasterization caches that coexist with projection and gradient state at peak memory. A complete-view update aggregates gradients across the view; each region's forward and backward caches can be released after its contribution is collected. BoundedGS separates rasterization and projection backward passes and bounds the active local rasterization working set according to its measured load. Candidate-indexed projection and compact gradient storage address the view-level peaks exposed by this change, while CPU-assisted structure rebuilding and bounded image supply manage resources outside rendering. In a resolution sweep at a fixed count of about 6M Gaussians, the measured rendering working set stays within 1.073-1.077 GiB from 1K to 16K; at 11K, a warm pass takes 19.79 seconds versus 21.76 for full-frame execution. Across five native 5K outdoor scenes, full training reduces the mean rendering working set from 9.97 to 1.76 GiB (82.3%), retains similar reconstruction quality, and shortens training time from 36.7 to 33.9 minutes. Project page: https://xiaobin2001.github.io/BoundedGS-Web/
authors: Xiaobin Deng, Changyu Diao, Min Li, Duanqing Xu
bullets: High-resolution 3DGS exceeds memory limits because rasterization caches grow alongside projection and gradient state.

Across five native 5K outdoor scenes, rendering memory drops 82.3% while quality remains similar and training becomes faster.

papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction is important for embodied agents operating in complex environments whose semantic categories extend beyond fixed taxonomies. While recent studies have explored open-vocabulary occupancy in outdoor driving scenarios, indoor environments remain challenging due to dense occlusions, complex geometry, and fine-grained long-tailed semantics. To reduce the need for expensive voxel-level semantic annotations, we study a geometry-only supervision setting requiring only binary occupancy labels. We build upon Language-Embedded Gaussians as a unified representation coupling 3D geometry with language-aligned semantics. For geometry learning, we introduce an opacity-aware Poisson-based Gaussian-to-Occupancy formulation that enables stable volumetric aggregation under binary occupancy supervision. For semantic learning, we render Gaussian features into images and align them with a frozen open-vocabulary model, together with Progressive Temperature Decay to reduce feature mixing during Gaussian splatting. Building on this framework, we further introduce Instance-Level Semantic Consistency to alleviate fragmented object predictions, and Covisibility-Aware Support-View Selection to provide informative and less redundant multi-view semantic supervision. We also extend our framework to outdoor driving scenarios to evaluate its generality across substantially different environments. Extensive experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves strong open-vocabulary occupancy performance, validating the effectiveness and generality of our framework. Code will be available at https://github.com/JuIvyy/LegoOcc.
authors: Changqing Zhou, Yueru Luo, Han Zhang, Zeyu Jiang, Changhao Chen
bullets: Targets indoor and outdoor scenes with dense occlusions, complex geometry, and long-tailed semantics beyond fixed taxonomies.
Uses binary occupancy labels for geometry, with an opacity-aware Poisson Gaussian-to-occupancy formulation for stable volumetric aggregation.
Aligns rendered Gaussian features with a frozen open-vocabulary model and applies Progressive Temperature Decay to reduce feature mixing.
Introduces Instance-Level Semantic Consistency and Covisibility-Aware Support-View Selection to improve fragmented and redundant multi-view predictions.
Experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks show strong performance and cross-environment generality.

figures.caption: Fig. 2: Framework Overview. From a monocular image, a feed-forward Gaussian model produces Language-Embedded Gaussians. Training proceeds along two paths: Semantic learning, we differentiably render Gaussian features to the image with Progressive Temperature Decay and align them to a training-free open-vocabulary segmenter via a cosine objective Lfeat; Geometry learning, we convert Gaussians to occupancy using an opacity-aware Poisson-based Gaussian-to-Occupancy operator and supervise binary occupancy with Locc. At inference, the Language-Embedded Occupancy supports text-driven queries by computing cosine similarity between voxel embeddings and prompt embeddings, yielding open-vocabulary semantic occupancy without dense voxel-level semantic labels during training.

Fig. 6: Qualitative results on Occ-ScanNet. From top to bottom: (a) input images; (b) ground-truth semantic occupancy; (c) results from our re-implemented LOcc [23]; (d) LegoOcc; and (e) LegoOcc++. All compared open-vocabulary methods are trained with geometry-only supervision and evaluated using the closed-vocabulary annotations of Occ-ScanNet.

Fig. 5: Covisibility-aware support-view selection. Each example shows a reference view (left) and four support views. Fixed temporal selection often produces highly redundant observations (top). Our method filters views with either insufficient overlap or near-duplicate content according to geometric covisibility, and selects pose-diverse views from the remaining candidates (bottom), providing complementary observations while preserving shared scene geometry.

Fig. 1: Closed- vs. open-vocabulary occupancy. Conventional closed-vocabulary methods [5], [6] can recognize only categories predefined during training. In contrast, our openvocabulary formulation aligns language with 3D occupancy and supports text queries for arbitrary categories. Right column (Random Class): text-conditioned voxel scores are visualized as heatmaps, where darker red indicates a higher response to the queried category.

Fig. 7: Open-vocabulary qualitative comparison. Legends list the VLM-extracted object nouns used as text queries. (a) Input image. (b) Open-vocabulary 2D segmentation for the queried nouns. (c) LegoOcc 3D open-vocabulary occupancy, colored by the same categories. (d) LegoOcc++ 3D open-vocabulary occupancy, colored by the same categories.

Fig. 3: Comparison of temperature schedules. Linear decay decreases τ uniformly, whereas our exponential schedule rapidly approaches Tmin, allocating more iterations for the model to adapt to the low-temperature regime.

Fig. 8: Qualitative results on Occ3D-nuScenes. We show surround-view input images and semantic occupancy predictions from GaussTR and LegoOcc++, together with the ground truth. LegoOcc++ better preserves the overall road layout and longrange scene structure, yielding more complete occupancy predictions.

Fig. 4: Instance-level semantic consistency. Given an input image (left), a frozen open-vocabulary teacher (e.g., Trident [36]) provides semantic cues in image space (middle), which can be spatially fragmented and incomplete for the same object. In contrast, SAM produces category-agnostic instance masks (right) that more coherently capture complete object extents. We aggregate teacher features within each reliable SAM mask to form an instance-level semantic prototype, and encourage rendered LE-Gaussian features inside the same instance to align with this shared prototype.

TABLE II: Quantitative performance of 3D occupancy methods on the Occ3D-nuScenes dataset. We compare methods that do not rely on LiDAR supervision. Frames denotes the number of temporal frames required at inference, and methods requiring more than one frame are shown in gray. IoU scores for “others” and “other flat” classes are consistently zero and thus omitted. “Cons. veh.” denotes construction vehicles, and “drive. surf.” denotes drivable surfaces.

For POP-3D, we project voxel centers to the image plane and sample language-aligned features at those locations to form a 3D grid of text-aligned embeddings for open-vocabulary reasoning. papers.abstract: Deep learning facilitates rapid single shot three dimensional (3D) reconstruction using fringe projection profilometry (FPP), but recovering accurate surface height from a single high frequency fringe image remains challenging because both long-range spatial consistency and fine geometric details must be preserved. Convolutional networks are limited in modeling long range dependencies, whereas window-based Transformers establish global interactions only progressively with increasing depth. To address these limitations, a hybrid Mamba Transformer network is proposed for fringe to height regression. The network adopts a Swin based U shaped architecture and introduces visual state space modeling at the intermediate resolution encoder stage. An axial and dilated vision state space (ADVSS) block is further developed to enhance prescan feature encoding through local, dilated, and axial depthwise convolutions while retaining four directional selective scanning. This design combines linear complexity long range modeling with direction aware preservation of local fringe structures. Experiments on a publicly available FPP dataset show that the proposed method outperforms hNet, SwinConvUNet, UHRNet, and HiDNet in mean absolute error(MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), absolute relative error, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Using only one deformed fringe image, the proposed method achieves an RMSE of 0.548 mm and an SSIM of 0.9985, reducing RMSE by 65.2% and 59.6% relative to UHRNet and HiDNet, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining selective state space modeling with hierarchical window based attention for accurate single-shot FPP reconstruction.
bullets: Addresses the difficulty of preserving both global spatial consistency and fine geometric details in single-shot fringe projection profilometry.
Uses a Swin-based U-shaped encoder–decoder with visual state space modeling at an intermediate resolution.
Introduces an axial and dilated vision state space block with local, dilated, and axial convolutions plus four-directional selective scanning.
On a public FPP dataset, outperforms hNet, SwinConvUNet, UHRNet, and HiDNet across MAE, RMSE, absolute relative error, and SSIM.
Achieves 0.548 mm RMSE and 0.9985 SSIM from a single deformed fringe image; evaluation is limited to the reported public dataset and metrics.

papers.abstract: Language-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has advanced language-driven 3D scene understanding by incorporating semantic and relational cues into reconstructed scenes. However, relation-aware grounding depends not only on representing such information, but also on whether the underlying scene-side evidence is reliable and sufficient. Multi-view semantic aggregation can incorporate weak observations, while object relations can remain under-observed along the available camera trajectory, leading to ambiguous evidence for target disambiguation. We present RelateGS, a structured language-aware Gaussian representation that selectively refines semantic and relational evidence for 3D visual grounding. RelateGS suppresses unreliable observations during semantic feature uplifting and consolidates multi-view object observations into a persistent 3D graph. The graph further identifies under-observed object relations and guides targeted re-querying of informative existing frames to complement their evidence. Experiments on Sr3D+ and Nr3D demonstrate competitive 3D grounding performance, improving the previous best by 7.9 and 1.7 percentage points at Acc@0.25, respectively.
bullets: Addresses ambiguous target disambiguation caused by weak semantic observations and incomplete relational evidence.
Suppresses unreliable multi-view observations during semantic feature uplifting.
Builds a persistent 3D object-relation graph from multi-view observations.
Uses the graph to identify missing relations and re-query informative existing frames.
Improves prior best Acc@0.25 by 7.9 points on Sr3D+ and 1.7 points on Nr3D.

figures.caption: Figure 2. Overview of RelateGS. At the object level, multi-view observations are consolidated into a persistent graph, whose current state identifies under-observed object pairs and guides targeted re-querying of informative existing frames.

For each method, green denotes the ground-truth target, yellow indicates a correctly grounded prediction, and red indicates an incorrect prediction. Compared with language-embedded Gaussian representations and RelateGS without relational re-querying (w/o RQ), the full RelateGS more reliably resolves targets from relational expressions by complementing underobserved relational evidence.

Figure 1. Motivation of RelateGS. Existing methods can suffer from (A) unreliable semantic evidence due to weak multiview observations and (B) insufficient relational evidence due to limited viewpoint coverage. RelateGS addresses these issues by (A) filtering weak observations during semantic feature uplifting and (B) complementing under-observed relations through graphguided re-querying of informative existing views.

papers.abstract: Unrolled variational networks achieve state-of-the-art performance for accelerated MRI reconstruction, but standard end-to-end training becomes prohibitively memory intensive as the number and width of cascades increase. We propose a memory-efficient training framework that updates a randomly sampled cascade while retaining supervision from the final reconstruction loss. The error signal is propagated from the end of the chain to the sampled cascade using an activation-light backward pass that avoids storing full chain activations, thereby decoupling training memory from chain length. A time-conditioned network shared across cascades further keeps the parameter count independent of chain length. The backward pass is approximate only through frozen normalization statistics, and a trained exact gradient control shows the approximation leaves reconstruction quality unchanged. The framework remains trainable at chain lengths and cascade widths where standard end-to-end backpropagation exhausts GPU memory. On fastMRI single-coil knee and multi-coil brain reconstruction, our method consistently outperforms other local training approaches. On high-SNR knee slices, our method surpasses E2E-VarNet at $8\times$ and matches it at $4\times$, while on the complete brain validation set it surpasses E2E-VarNet at $8\times$ and achieves comparable performance at $4\times$, with fewer parameters, lower peak memory, and faster per-iteration training. Code is available at https://github.com/emehillaj/scalable-unrolled-mri.
bullets: Randomly samples a cascade for updating while retaining supervision from the final reconstruction loss.
Uses an activation-light backward pass to propagate error without memory scaling with chain length.
Shares a time-conditioned network across cascades, keeping parameter count independent of chain length.
Maintains reconstruction quality despite approximate gradients caused by frozen normalization statistics.
Outperforms other local-training methods and matches or exceeds E2E-VarNet in the reported fastMRI knee and brain settings, with fewer parameters, lower peak memory, and faster iteration training.

papers.abstract: Reconstructing a coherent 3D scene from uncurated image collections remains challenging due to the presence of irrelevant or non-overlapping views. Recent work has shown that feed-forward reconstruction models contain internal view-consistency signals that support distractor rejection. However, reference-conditioned filtering relies on a curated clean reference, which is not guaranteed in practical image collections. To address this limitation, we introduce FreeView, a training-free framework that jointly selects a filtering reference and rejects distractor views from an uncurated collection. FreeView leverages collection-level consensus to identify a representative view that serves as a reliable reference for filtering. It then adapts view rejection to each input collection by combining complementary visual and geometric evidence. This approach preserves useful views under substantial appearance and viewpoint variations while rejecting distractors. FreeView integrates with both VGGT and pi^3, removing the need for a manually curated reference or manual calibration of view rejection. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate high clean-view retention and distractor rejection rates, leading to reliable 3D reconstruction from uncurated views.
authors: Junho Kim, Hyunyoung Choi, Seongwon Lee
bullets: Addresses irrelevant and non-overlapping views that can disrupt reconstruction.
Uses collection-level consensus to select a representative filtering reference.
Combines visual and geometric evidence to adapt view rejection to each collection.
Integrates with VGGT and pi^3 while preserving useful views under appearance and viewpoint variation.
Experiments across multiple datasets show high clean-view retention and distractor rejection, improving reconstruction reliability.

figures.caption: Fig. 2: Overview of FreeView. Given an uncurated image collection, Consensus Reference Selection identifies a representative view through agreement among related images, establishing a reference for filtering without prior knowledge of which views are clean. Adaptive Dual-Cue Rejection combines complementary visual and geometric evidence to adapt view selection to each collection. Retaining views supported by either cue preserves useful observations under appearance and viewpoint variations, while rejecting views unsupported by both suppresses distractors. The retained views are then processed by VGGT or π3 for final reconstruction.

papers.abstract: Counterfactual cardiac anatomy can support risk modelling and intervention planning, by predicting how a patient's heart would change under altered clinical conditions. However, current shape generative models are conditional on clinical variables and disregard causal links between these variables. Thus, they cannot answer counterfactual questions about how a given subject's anatomy would change under a different clinical profile. Modelling the heart's continuous movement over the cardiac cycle requires a representation that is itself continuous in space and time. Spatio-temporal neural distance fields provide this while separating clinical conditioning from subject-specific shape. We place a structural causal model (SCM) over the set of clinical variables (age, sex, smoking, BMI, heart rate, systolic blood pressure), before the condition encoding of the spatio-temporal neural distance field which represents the left atrial complex over a cardiac cycle by signed distance fields. An intervention of the clinical variables, propagated through a SCM before the 4D counterfactual, is constructed from the neural distance field. The generated counterfactuals follow dose-response under age interventions and transforms the male distribution to closely match the female distribution under the intervention $\mathrm{do(\mathrm{female}{=}1)}$. By doing inverse interventions the model also approximates the original anatomy with sub millimeter precision. To our knowledge, this is the first counterfactual generation of 4D cardiac anatomy and the first integration of an SCM with an implicit neural representation as its imaging mechanism.
bullets: Addresses the inability of conventional shape generators to model causal relationships or answer subject-level counterfactual anatomy questions.
Uses a structural causal model over age, sex, smoking, BMI, heart rate, and systolic blood pressure before a continuous spatio-temporal signed-distance-field representation.
Models the left atrial complex continuously across space and the cardiac cycle while separating clinical conditioning from subject-specific shape.
Produces dose-responsive age interventions and shifts male anatomy toward the female distribution under an intervention on sex.
Inverse interventions recover the original anatomy with submillimeter precision; the work is presented as the first SCM-integrated implicit model for counterfactual 4D cardiac anatomy.
